quoted_clause: PIES is the subset of those candidate classes with ≥1 guardrail bypass in the cycle
observed: The text defines 217 as the candidate pattern space (CPS) and defines PIES as the subset of CPS with at least one guardrail bypass, but the mini-case and Table 24-1 later use 217 as the PIES value.
evidence: §3.1 says CPS = 217 and PIES is the bypass subset. §8 says PIES dropped from 217 to 143, and Table 24-1 lists PIES = 217 in Cycle 1. If 217 is CPS, it is not necessarily PIES unless every candidate class bypassed at least one guardrail in Cycle 1.
root_cause: Conflation of the candidate pattern space (all deduplicated probe classes) with the bypassed-pattern count (PIES).
correction: Either define PIES as the CPS and introduce a separate bypassed-pattern metric, or explicitly state that in Cycle 1 all 217 candidate classes had at least one bypass so PIES = CPS = 217, and that 143/138 are bypassed-class counts.
acceptance_test: Every occurrence of PIES refers to the same quantity; if 217 is CPS, Table 24-1 labels it CPS or the text states PIES=CPS for Cycle 1.

quoted_clause: False-positive rate | FACT | Share of guardrail interventions that block legitimate user intent
observed: Several metrics defined as shares, rates, or percentages are labeled FACT, but they are computed from lower-level observed counts.
evidence: False-positive rate is a share of interventions; tool-use exploit rate is a percentage of probes; guardrail-trigger rate is interventions per 1,000 queries. These are derived quantities, not raw observed events.
root_cause: The Type column treats computed rates as FACT instead of DERIVED.
correction: Mark ratio/rate metrics as DERIVED, or split each metric into a raw FACT count and a DERIVED rate.
acceptance_test: No metric whose definition is a share, percentage, or per-1000 rate is labeled FACT unless the raw count is separately identified as the FACT.

quoted_clause: samples 1,000 retrievals per cycle (n ≈ 1,000 sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; 0.001 resolution)
observed: The sample-size rationale is under-specified and may be statistically incorrect if it means a ±0.001 absolute 95% confidence margin.
evidence: For p ≈ 0.003, a 95% margin of ±0.001 requires roughly n ≈ 1.96^2 * p(1-p) / 0.001^2 ≈ 11,500. n = 1,000 does support a rule-of-three style statement that zero observed poisoned retrievals gives an upper 95% bound near 0.003, but that is not the same as 0.001 resolution.
root_cause: The text conflates target detection, absolute resolution, and confidence-bound semantics.
correction: State the intended statistical claim. For example: 1,000 retrievals makes one poisoned retrieval a 0.001 increment, and zero observed hits gives an approximate 95% upper bound of 0.003; or increase n if a ±0.001 95% CI is required.
acceptance_test: The stated n, confidence level, and resolution form one consistent statistical claim.

quoted_clause: 40 rps × 8.6 s = 344 in-flight × 24.9 GB ÷ 436 GB = 19.7 → 21 hosts
observed: The continuous arithmetic gives 19.7 hosts, which would round/ceil to 20, not 21. The 21-host result depends on the conservative integer floor of 17 concurrent requests per host, which is not shown in this sentence.
evidence: 436 GB / 24.9 GB ≈ 17.51, floor 17. 344 / 17 ≈ 20.24, ceil 21. The same section also says Candidate B's 8 hosts hold 140 in-flight using 17.5, mixing the continuous 17.5 with the conservative 17-based host count.
root_cause: Omitted integer-floor step in the peak KV-residency screen.
correction: Show the conservative path explicitly: 436 / 24.9 = 17.51 → floor 17 concurrent requests/host; 344 / 17 ≈ 20.2 → 21 hosts. Or distinguish the continuous 19.7 estimate from the conservative 21-host screen.
acceptance_test: The printed 21-host value follows from a visible arithmetic path using the same concurrency assumption.

quoted_clause: Candidate A: 4×H100 hosts, 8-bit KV, tight batching target (batch ≤ 8), minimal headroom. Looks cheap: 4 hosts is half the aggregate compute and HBM of Candidate B.
observed: The notation 4×H100 hosts is ambiguous: it can be read as four H100 GPUs total, but the surrounding text means four hosts, each an 8×H100 node.
evidence: Later in the same section, one 8×H100 host is said to provide 7.9 PFLOP/s, and Candidate B is described as 8 hosts. The comparison is 4 hosts versus 8 hosts, not 4 GPUs versus 8 GPUs.
root_cause: Missing host/GPU distinction in the candidate labels.
correction: Write 4 8×H100 hosts and 8 8×H100 hosts, or 4 H100-8 hosts and 8 H100-8 hosts, so the unit is unambiguous.
acceptance_test: A reader cannot interpret Candidate A as a 4-GPU system.

page_hint: Chapter 25, ADR 0015 Context and Requirement R1
observed: ADR 0015 uses both 10 rps average load and 6.24M requests/month as canonical values, but those are not dimensionally consistent for a 30-day month.
evidence: 10 rps × 86,400 s/day × 30 days = 25.92M requests/month. 6.24M requests/month corresponds to 6.24M / 2,592,000 s ≈ 2.4 rps average. The $/1K figures are derived from 6.24M, so the rate/volume mismatch propagates into cost-per-request.
root_cause: Mixed canonical volume basis: 10 rps average is paired with a monthly volume that implies a lower average rate.
correction: Choose one canonical basis. If 6.24M requests/month is canonical, state the implied average rate or duty cycle and adjust the 10 rps label. If 10 rps average is canonical, recompute the monthly volume and all $/1K values.
acceptance_test: The R1 request rate and the monthly request volume are consistent under the stated month length and duty cycle.

page_hint: Chapter 25, §7 What We Still Don't Know
quoted_clause: Each item below is a hypothesis awaiting verification — none has FACT instrumentation yet:
observed: The section introduction says every item is a hypothesis awaiting verification and has no FACT instrumentation, but the Tooling gaps item is explicitly labeled [1P][FACT].
evidence: The same section contains: Tooling gaps: [1P][FACT] — no widely adopted tool exists for ADR graph visualization or impact analysis (a factual tooling observation, not an open hypothesis).
root_cause: A factual tooling observation was left inside a section framed as open hypotheses.
correction: Either reword the introduction to include factual tooling observations, or move the Tooling gaps item out of the unknowns section into a factual note.
acceptance_test: No item labeled [FACT] appears under a heading that says every item is a hypothesis awaiting verification.

page_hint: Chapter 25, ADR 0015 Requirement R1 and R4
quoted_clause: 70% × 95% + N−1 policy: 32 (KV screen) / 34 (case (ii) prefill screen, Ch 20)
observed: The policy row says 32 hosts for the KV screen, and R4 describes that as a 32-host policy row with 31 working plus 1 reserve. If 31 hosts are working, the stated 70% × 95% derating does not clearly close to the 21-host KV screen.
evidence: 21 / (0.7 × 0.95) ≈ 31.58. Rounding up gives 32 working hosts, and adding N−1 reserve would make 33 total. If 32 is total with 31 working, 31 × 0.7 × 0.95 ≈ 20.6, below 21.
root_cause: Ambiguity over whether 32 is the working-host count or the total host count, and whether rounding occurs before or after adding the N−1 reserve.
correction: State the policy arithmetic explicitly, for example: 21 / 0.665 = 31.58 → 32 working hosts, plus 1 reserve = 33 total; or adjust the factors/rounding rule so 32 total is defensible.
acceptance_test: The working-host count, reserve count, and derating factors close to the underlying 21/22-host screens without an unexplained off-by-one.

quoted_clause: it does halve the KV-read bytes, a secondary ~15% term
observed: The phrase can be read as saying that halving KV-read bytes saves ~15% of decode memory traffic, but the ~15% figure is the KV component's share of total decode reads, not the total reduction from halving that component.
evidence: For a 70B FP16 model at 9,500 tokens, weight reads are ~140 GB and KV reads are ~24.9 GB. KV is 24.9 / (140 + 24.9) ≈ 15.1% of total reads. Halving KV reduces total reads by 12.45 / 164.9 ≈ 7.5%.
root_cause: The percentage scope is ambiguous: component share versus total traffic reduction.
correction: Write: KV reads are a ~15% component of decode memory traffic at this context length; halving them reduces total decode read traffic by ~7.5%.
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer that FP8 KV gives a 15% total decode-bandwidth saving.

page_hint: Chapter 25, §6 Architecture Consequence, Integration with CI
quoted_clause: ensuring every ADR has a status, a rationale, and at least one evidence tag
observed: The CI validation mentions a rationale field, but the copy-ready template in §3.1 does not include an explicit Rationale section.
evidence: The template has Status, Decision, Architecture Decision Context, Alternatives considered, Evidence, Trade-offs & consequences, Decision owner, Validation plan, Rollback plan, Review trigger, and Falsification path. The worked ADR has Rationale, but the template does not.
root_cause: The CI rule references a field that is not present in the canonical template.
correction: Add a Rationale section to the template, or change the CI check to require context/evidence/trade-off fields that actually exist in the template.
acceptance_test: Every field required by the CI rule appears in the copy-ready template.

quoted_clause: excluding that term entirely (a 400 ms baseline) would report (400 − 250) / 400 = 37.5% instead.
observed: The alternative 37.5% calculation is not like-for-like: the 250 ms miss value includes the 50 ms retrieval term, while the 400 ms baseline excludes it.
evidence: Step 2 defines the miss path as 120 + 80 + 50 = 250 ms. If the 50 ms retrieval term is excluded entirely from both paths, the miss path is 120 + 80 = 200 ms and the reduction is (400 − 200) / 400 = 50%. If the miss path remains 250 ms, the baseline should remain 450 ms for the 44% comparison.
root_cause: Inconsistent component set in the alternative percentage.
correction: Replace the sentence with a consistent comparison: either keep retrieval in both paths and report (450 − 250) / 450 ≈ 44%, or exclude retrieval from both paths and report (400 − 200) / 400 = 50%.
acceptance_test: The numerator and denominator in every percentage use the same latency components.

page_hint: Chapter 26, §8 Step 0 and Fig 26.1 provenance note
quoted_clause: reads the capstone's workload against Fig 26.1 — a short-prompt, latency-sensitive RAG workload, closest to the matrix's short-input latency-bound rows
observed: Fig 26.1 scores the canonical long-context RAG Q&A family, not the capstone's distinct short-prompt RAG workload. The capstone is later declared not to be the canonical 9.2K-input case, so using Fig 26.1 as if it represents the capstone's short-prompt RAG workload is misleading.
evidence: The Fig 26.1 provenance note gives long-context RAG Q&A a context-length score of 0.95 and output-token score of 0.45. Step 1 explicitly says the capstone is a distinct short-prompt workload, not the canonical 9.2K-input/1.08-s-prefill case.
root_cause: Mismatch between the figure's scored workload families and the capstone's declared short-prompt workload.
correction: Clarify that the capstone is not the Fig 26.1 long-context RAG point; either add a short-prompt RAG fingerprint or say the capstone is closest to the matrix's short-input latency-bound rows rather than to Fig 26.1's RAG Q&A bar.
acceptance_test: Step 0's reference to Fig 26.1 matches the actual workload being analyzed.
